issues.description: FAQ example conflates Content-Length with body length without stating the invariant
issues.detail: The handler reads min(content_length, available) and treats a non-empty read as 201, empty as 400. The author has not stated what 'empty body with non-zero Content-Length' means at the protocol level. Is this a malformed request (400 by spec), a truncated stream, or simulator artifact? Without a precondition, the test asserts vibes, not behavior. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: Switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream is asserted without justification
issues.detail: things_advanced.py changes body = req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read(). These have different preconditions: bounded_stream enforces Content-Length, stream does not. The diff offers no reasoning for why this change is correct, nor what postcondition it preserves. If the change is required to make the new test pass, that is precisely the smell: the production code was bent to fit the test.

issues.description: README diff smuggles unrelated refactors into a test PR
issues.detail: The PR title promises POST tests for things_advanced. The README diff rewrites StorageError.handle signature (ex,req,resp -> req,resp,ex), swaps str(status_code)+reason for code_to_http_status, and changes stream to bounded_stream. These are semantic changes hidden inside a cosmetic reformatting. A reviewer cannot audit correctness when the frame of the change is undeclared. REFUSED on scope grounds.

issues.description: Test asserts status codes without specifying the property under test
issues.detail: test_things_advanced now appends two POST cases. Neither has a comment stating what invariant of the example is being verified. resp3 checks the happy path; resp4 checks that an empty body with Content-Length:1 yields 400. The latter only holds because of the bounded_stream change. The test and the code under test were modified together to converge; the postcondition was never written down.

issues.description: FAQ test uses assert(result.status == ...) — parenthesized assert is a known Python footgun
issues.detail: assert(expr) reads like a function call and silently passes when given a tuple. The example will mislead readers who copy it. Trivial to fix: assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400. Documentation code is read more than it is run; correctness of the example matters.

issues.description: FAQ example's control flow is nested where it should be flat
issues.detail: if content_length in (None,0): 200 else: if stream.read(...): 201 else: 400. Three disjoint cases written as nested selection. A guarded sequence of three returns would make the postcondition readable. Minor, but the FAQ is teaching idiom; teach the structured form.

review.summary: The PR claims to add POST tests but quietly mutates the example under test (req.stream to req.bounded_stream) so that the new failing case becomes 400. Code and test were adjusted together; no precondition, postcondition, or invariant was stated for either the example or the FAQ snippet. TESTED-NOT-PROVED. The README diff smuggles unrelated semantic changes (handler signature, status formatting) under a reformatting commit, which a correctness review cannot accept. The FAQ snippet additionally contains a parenthesized assert and unnecessarily nested control flow. Reason about the spec, then write the test; do not bend the program to make the assertion green.
